scope_statement: GCSE Latin, summer 2027 examination series. The literature and sources themes in scope are 'Heroes and Villains' (Cicero Philippic 2.118-119; Livy History 2.10; Propertius Elegy 4.6; Sallust Bellum Catilinae 25; Tacitus Annals 4.1 and 4.59; Virgil Aeneid 8.478-495; Virgil Aeneid 11.648-689) and 'Come Dine with Me!' (Aulus Gellius Attic Nights 2.24; Juvenal Satire 11.64-80; Martial Epigrams 3.60; Ovid Metamorphoses 1.221-239 and 8.664-688; Petronius Cena Trimalchionis 31-34 adapted; Pliny Letters 2.6; Seneca de Clementia 1.18). The narratives in scope are Livy 'Hannibal crosses the Alps' (Livy 21) and Virgil 'Hercules and Cacus' (Aeneid 8.152-336). The Roman civilisation topics in scope are 'Slavery in the Roman World' and 'Roman Festivals and Worship'. Anything from the retired 2024-2026 prescriptions is OUT OF SCOPE: the themes 'Romans in the Countryside' and 'Love and Marriage', the narratives Suetonius 'Nero' and Ovid 'The Adventures of Perseus', and the civilisation topics 'Roman family life' and 'The City of Rome'. Flag as HIGH any lesson that teaches retired material as though it were assessed. The language component is unseen: no set text applies to it.
